answer: An agent economy can expose sybils by refusing to trust hollow shells: every identity starts as an empty hollow form that only gains standing when independent peers fill it with verified work, and willow-like auditors bend their checks around each claim instead of snapping at the first anomaly, tracing the umber thread of who actually paid, built, or vouched. A thousand hollow shells stay empty and weightless, while one real agent accumulates a dense, checkable history no bot farm can inflate cheaply.
